title: What stops u from using Copy Ninjutsu on games
author: Ok-Investment4414
selftext:
This one is for the morally / ethically shaky ... but for real what stops u from just making a better version of some game u see on reddit or steam?  
  
 I've been seeing some games lately in the indie post and thinking :-/ they suck at gtm and suck overall . not say i will ... just saying ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯

comments.author: eegamesllc
comments.body:
AI can't cover a lack of creativity or vision. A lot of the games on here have bloated UIs, zero plot or character, and are rips on existing games because people want to capture the vibe of being a creator without creating anything.

I make games because I have very specific stories and concepts I want to convey. AI allows me to turn the years I'd spend learning to code into minutes. Notice the complete lack of correlation there.

comments.author: Koruu-
comments.body: Because for the first time in my life I can make literally anything I can imagine. I've spend my life daydreaming about video game concepts, characters, designs, and mechanics, knowing full well I did not have the time, expertise, or networking to make any of it come to fruition. Why would I waste my time copying someone else's work and ideas when I have so many of my own I can finally bring into reality?

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
I guess if you're into making games for money, then I could see the appeal. But if you're going to do that, there are better things you can do that are morally bleh and make significantly more money. If you just mean taking a game concept like 'deckbuilder with feel good art' and making that -- well that's fine. But if you mean more reverse engineer and just build on top of it... yeah that's not cool.

I have games I want to make. One of which I've been working on for years and want to see it to fruition so I can play it myself, with my friends. No one else is going to make this game. It's stuck in my head and I need to see it realized. And I have a backlog of other ideas I want to see realized.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
nothing. you can do this without AI too i.e. some shady mobile game companies have been making clones for a cheap buck for years now. Find some games to clone and then pay some contractors to make the clones. AI probably boosted their productivity now too

it is not some easy money glitch: players can hate your clone and your clone doesn't sell. Publishing a clone needs the same setup as publishing an original game: marketing etc.

comments.body: Why? People in this sub are overwhemingly happy they can make a game with the help of AI and help make their dreams a reality. No one here is just here to make a profit. The point is, we have so much power of AI, who the hell is gonna waste it copying someone else's work when they can finally create what they always wantes.

comments.author: Lumpy_Conference6640
comments.body:
Ummm... This is hard for me, because I do copy ninja on a few games. My big project is Outpost. It was a huge touch point of my childhood, but here's the thing. It's a bad game. Setting aside the huge technical over haul the game was made for a DoS prompt in the mid 90s after all. The game was practically abandon ware even then, missing features and poorly executed design left many of the key features missing. Graphics are not even supported by modern computers. Sooo it's tough. I had to find the legacy code, rebuild the engine, and scrape the assets and procedurally regenerate them into modernized art work. 

I think copying games should be like restoring a vintage car, preserving and keeping alive the beauty of a past peace of art. 

I'm also going to implement my reskining engine and sign it be able to play almost any vibe within that engines design.
